facility.name: La Petite Toepperwein
facility.programs_provided: Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 829 TOEPPERWEIN RD, CONVERSE, TX, 78109

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: There were two files that did not have health care provider statements signed at the time of review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - Letter or form from the most recent Licensing Inspection or Investigation: The operation did not have the most recent inspection form posted at time of review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - Letter or form from the most recent Licensing Inspection or Investigation (26 TAC §746.401(2))

occurrences.finding: Notification of Additional Services Offered: The operation did not notify CCR that they were offering transportation services.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Notification of Additional Services Offered (26 TAC §746.301(7))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the walk through of the playground, there were three children inside a gate around the wall while the teacher was tending to a child that did not want to leave the playground.     *Operation put a carabiner on the gate to not let it open*
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: A caregiver did not know the number of children in their care after combining classes for nap time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: During the investigation process, a caregiver did not follow the operational procedures for doing hourly name to face checks, did not have the name to face checks verified by another staff member, and did not follow the protocols set in place when the operation is short staffed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §746.201(1))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: During the investigation process, it was determined that the infant classroom was out of ratio when a caregiver left the room leaving one caregiver with five infants under twelve months old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregivers did not use good judgment when they did not contact EMS after finding a 3 year old child on the playground with no jacket.  The child had been on unattended on the playground for over 2 hours.  Temperatures that day ranged from 23 degrees to 34 degrees Fahrenheit
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Notify Immediately about Allegation of Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation: The operation did not notify the parents immediately about their child being left on the playground.  The parent was notified several hours after the incident occurred.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Notify Immediately about Allegation of Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation (26 TAC §746.307(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for: During the investigation process, a caregiver did not know the number of children that were in their care at drop off time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know number of children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During the investigation process, a caregiver did not maintain supervision of a child.  The child was able to leave the classroom, go through another classroom, open the door to the playground and enter the playground unattended.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: An infants hands were not washed after their diaper was changed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: Two caregivers did not have administering medication training at the time of review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: At time of inspection, the school aged class was observed to have cleaning solutions at childrens reach.     THis was corrected at inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments: It is found though investigation evidence a staff was assigned a classroom when they did not have the skills to safely supervise the entire group in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employee Assignments (26 TAC §746.1003(3))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: The loose fill under 2 slides is not 6 inches deep during the inspection.  note: This was corrected during the inspection when the loose fill was redistributed under the slides.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: Nap cots in the PreK room do not have labels on the cots reflecting the current children using the cots during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Based on evidence collected during this investigation, it was determined that the operation staff failed to respond appropriately to a child's symptoms of illness. The child was seen in the classroom laying on the floor coughing, and observed to be what was described as burning, yet no temperature was taken or first aid given by staff.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Child Becomes Ill in Care - Contact Parent: Based on evidence collected during this investigation, it was determined that the operation failed to ensure that a parent was contacted after discovering a child was displaying multiple symptoms of illness preventing the child from participating comfortably in activates.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child Becomes Ill in Care - Contact Parent (26 TAC §746.3605(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: During investigation, it was determined based on the video footage a child was separated from the group for more than 2 minutes, approximately 3 minutes, exceeding the one minute per year of the child?s age.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: It is found a child was left unsupervised for 7 minutes in a classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Immunizations-Immunization record must include the child's name and birth date: Two of ten children's files did not include a current immunization record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunizations-Immunization record must include the child's name and birth date (26 TAC §746.623(1)(A))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training: While reviewing traning records. Two of sixteen employee files did not include verification of Pre Service Training as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: While reviewing the monthly infant feeding schedules, six of eight schedules were not updated within the last thirty days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Per inv#3095466--standdard found deficient.  Updating additional inv inspection report of pending standard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During an investigation, it was determined that a caregiver knowingly allowed children to remain outside of visual and auditory awareness while attending to other duties in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Based on the interviews conducted, a caregiver did not conduct a name to face while lining the children up inside the classroom and when arriving outside before the children start to play to ensure all children were accounted for.  This resulted in a child being left in the classroom unsupervised for approximately 12 minutes.    Based on the interviews conducted, five children between ages 18 months and 2 years old were left on the playground by a caregiver with another caregiver watching the children from a distance from a classroom in the doorway.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on the interviews conducted a parent was not notified immediately when a child was left in a classroom unsupervised.  The parent was notified at pick-up.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: One child's file reviewed did not contain an immunization record.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Fire Extinguishers Serviced: The fire extinguishers in both vans used for transportation have not been serviced in the last year.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Extinguishers Serviced (26 TAC §746.5307(b))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: At the time of inspection there were 11 children with one caregiver in the 18 to 24 month old classroom.  This was corrected when a second caregiver joined the group.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: The walls in the toddler room and four year old classroom and the two year old classroom have peeling paint.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: The walls in each classroom have peeling paint.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: A fire drill has not been conducted since May.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Each classroom was dirty and in need of cleaning.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: At the time of inspection there were pieces of shredded plastic food wrap on the floor in the 12 to 24 month old classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2501(5))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings: At the time of inspection, the pole is bent in the fence that separates the toddler and older playground causing an entrapment hazard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Entrapment Openings (26 TAC §746.4601(3))

occurrences.finding: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually: Three driver's safety and transportation training certificates were expired.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Transportation Safety Training -Director and Employee Complete 2 Hours Annually (26 TAC §746.1316(a))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: At the time of inspection the playground surfacing was not maintained at the proper depth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Three childrens records reviewed did not contain immunization records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: At the time of inspection there were eight children's records reviewed that did not contain health statements.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: At the time of inspection the playground surfacing was not maintained at the proper depth.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Written Activity Plans: There were two classrooms that did not have the current activity plan available for review.   This was corrected when the plans were printed and posted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Activity Plans (26 TAC §746.2203(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: Investigation information obtained from DFPS Child Care Licensing investigator determined there was a child injured while in care at the operation when a caregiver sprayed a "cleaning" solution in the children's faces.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised: Investigation information obtained from DFPS Child Care Licensing investigator determined the caregivers are not adequately supervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Employees Supervised (26 TAC §746.1003(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: Investigation information obtained from DFPS Child Care Licensing investigator determined that the caregiver used inappropriate discipline when spraying the children in the face as a form of punishment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)
